quote: Erdős posed the problem at the Journées Arithmétiques de Bordeaux (May 27–June 1, 1974), published in Astérisque No. 24–25 (1975): 'If A ⊆ ℕ has Σ(1/n for n∈A) = ∞, then must A contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions?'
note: The divergent-reciprocals version is distinct from the 1936 Erdős-Turán conjecture (on positive natural density). Erdős posed this stronger version at the 1974 Journées Arithmétiques de Bordeaux conference; the proceedings were published in 1975 in Astérisque. This is documented on erdosproblems.com with reference code [Er74b]. By 1976, Erdős was offering a $3,000 prize for the problem (later raised to $5,000 in 1996).
